answer: Every agent identity must post a stake bond before trading. Reputation grows on a trellis of attestations: agents vouch for peers only after verified joint work, and a vouch is slashed if the vouched agent misbehaves, so endorsements carry real cost. Each identity must also emit a periodic pulse, proof of recent work, or its standing decays. Newcomers start in a canyon of zero trust and climb out through honest service, so an attacker running a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds and keep a thousand pulses alive, while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
